answer: Creating a fake identity costs a fresh cipher solve plus a forfeitable stake, while honest agents amortize costs across epochs. Each agent must solve a unique proof-of-work cipher tied to its identity, then stake a bond that decays along a registration vine rooted in a shared dune of prior attestations. Sybils multiply linearly in cost but only sublinearly in influence, so the dune of trust grows slower than the vine of fake registrations. In practice, Agent0009 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
